mechanism_claims.claim_text: Stapled anoplin analogs disrupt bacterial membrane integrity in a peptide- and species-dependent manner, measured by propidium iodide uptake in E. coli K12 MG1655 and S. aureus ATCC 29213.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: anoplin[2-6], anoplin[5-9], and related anoplin analogs

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=18:Monitoring Integrity of the Bacterial Membrane;xml:fig=1E-F

mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct assay supports membrane permeabilization/destructive effect; it does not distinguish a detailed pore model.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Hydrocarbon stapling increased helical structure/proteolytic stability and shifted activity: anoplin[2-6] was most active against Gram-negative strains while anoplin[5-9] was strongest against Gram-positive strains but more toxic.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: structure-activity relationship across Table 1, Table 2, Figure 1, Figure 2, and toxicity section
mechanism_claims.limitations: Structure/activity relationship is paper-supported but not a standalone direct molecular target assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper relates E. coli K12 activity to peptide helicity in LPS-containing membrane mimic conditions, but this is correlative context rather than direct LPS-binding quantification.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: anoplin analog helicity in LPS and E. coli K12 MIC relationship
mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not promote to direct LPS/endotoxin mechanism without a direct binding/disruption assay.

rejected_overclaims.reason: No paper-local assay in this article supports host immunomodulation as a mechanism for these peptides.
Only indirect helicity/MIC context in LPS mimic was available locally.
